assumptions.condition: \(\forall i\in V,\ \forall \mathbf z,\mathbf z'\in\{0,1\}^n:\ \mathbf z_{D_i}=\mathbf z'_{D_i}\Rightarrow Y_i(\mathbf z)=Y_i(\mathbf z')\).
\(\{Y_i(\mathbf z):i\in V,\mathbf z\in\{0,1\}^n\}\text{ is nonrandom under }P_{\ell}\).

novel.justification: A small set of brokers, market hubs, or cross-village connectors can contain every cycle while within-village residual contact structure is tree-like; the condition is directly checkable after the network is measured.

assumptions.condition: \(K_{\ell}(\pi)\ge 2\) for every \(\ell\in\{1,\ldots,L\}\) and every strict priority order \(\pi\) on \(V\).

novel.justification: The condition is equivalent to the conflict graph having no universal vertex and is satisfied by experiments spanning at least two disconnected villages or communities, since each component contributes a focal unit.

The graph-Sobolev ellipsoid allows arbitrary levels while controlling variation across conflict edges, a transparent sensitivity class for bounded or smoothly varying village-network endpoints after choosing a conservative radius.

definitions.name: WRI unit-isolation conflict graph
definitions.construction: \(C_G=(V,E_C)\), where \(\{i,j\}\in E_C\) if and only if \(i\ne j\) and \(D_i\cap D_j\ne\varnothing\).

definitions.name: Sequential weighted random isolation law
definitions.construction: Independently draw \(X_{\ell i}\) with density \(h_{\ell i}x^{h_{\ell i}-1}\) on \((0,1)\), scan vertices in decreasing \(X_{\ell i}\), and include a scanned vertex in \(S_{\ell}\) exactly when it has no previously included neighbor in \(C_G\).

definitions.name: Tagged isolated-count polynomial
definitions.construction: \(F_{\ell,A}(z)=\mathbb E_{\ell}[\mathbf 1\{A\subseteq S_{\ell}\}z^{K_{\ell}}]\), for every \(A\subseteq V\) with \(|A|\le2\).

definitions.name: Feedback-core WRI input class
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak C_k=\{(n,C_G,\mathcal K,h):n\ge2,\ |\mathcal K|=k,\ C_G-\mathcal K\text{ is a forest},\ h\in\{1,\ldots,b\}^{L\times n}\}\).

definitions.name: Three-state cutoff-forest messages
definitions.construction: Fix an independent \(\mathcal U\subseteq\mathcal K\), a blocker set \(\mathcal B\subseteq\mathcal K\setminus\mathcal U\), and core priorities \(x\in(0,1)^{\mathcal K}\). For \(v\notin\mathcal K\), put \(p_v(x)=\max(\{x_u:u\in\mathcal U\cap N_{C_G}(v)\}\cup\{0\})\) and \(r_v(x)=\min(\{x_f:f\in\mathcal B\cap N_{C_G}(v)\}\cup\{1\})\). Root each component of \(C_G-\mathcal K\). For a child \(w\) define \(J_w=\int_0^1B_w(t,z)\,dt\), \(D_w=\int_0^1(A_w(t,z)+B_w(t,z))\,dt\), and \(E_w(y)=J_w+\int_0^yA_w(t,z)\,dt\). With \(f_v(y)=h_{\ell v}y^{h_{\ell v}-1}\), set \(A_v(y,z)=zf_v(y)\mathbf 1\{N_{C_G}(v)\cap\mathcal U=\varnothing\}\mathbf 1\{y<r_v(x)\}\prod_w(J_w+\int_0^yC_w(t,z)\,dt)\), \(C_v(y,z)=f_v(y)\mathbf 1\{y\ge p_v(x)\}\prod_wE_w(y)\), and \(B_v(y,z)=f_v(y)\prod_wD_w-C_v(y,z)\); at a tagged forest vertex set \(B_v=C_v=0\).

definitions.name: Feedback-core inclusion-exclusion functional
definitions.construction: For a rooted forest component \(T\) with root \(v_T\), put \(P_{T;\mathcal U,\mathcal B,A}(x,z)=\int_0^1(A_{v_T}(y,z)+B_{v_T}(y,z))\,dy\) and \(\chi_{\mathcal U,\mathcal B}(x)=\mathbf 1\{x_u<x_f\text{ for every }f\in\mathcal B,\ u\in\mathcal U\cap N_{C_G}(f)\}\). Define \(\mathcal R_{\ell,A}(z)=\sum_{\substack{\mathcal U\subseteq\mathcal K\text{ independent}\\A\cap\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal U}}z^{|\mathcal U|}\sum_{\mathcal B\subseteq\mathcal K\setminus\mathcal U}(-1)^{|\mathcal B|}\int_{(0,1)^{\mathcal K}}\chi_{\mathcal U,\mathcal B}(x)\prod_{f\in\mathcal K}h_{\ell f}x_f^{h_{\ell f}-1}\prod_{T\in\operatorname{comp}(C_G-\mathcal K)}P_{T;\mathcal U,\mathcal B,A}(x,z)\,dx\).

definitions.name: Ordered-ratio evaluated moment handle
definitions.construction: For each of the at most \(k!\) strict core-priority chambers, substitute ordered ratios \(t_r=x_r/x_{r+1}\) for \(r<k\) and \(t_k=x_k\). Starting from the nested-moment recurrence for identical attachments, construct a finite operator algebra indexed only by core order types, tag states, and shared future-prefix transformations; require direct rational routines for child multiplication, component multiplication, moving-endpoint integration, and coefficient extraction, with no stored vector of \(k\) independent degree totals and no unevaluated integration gate.

definitions.name: Directed-realizable replicated-star stress test
definitions.construction: Let \(\mathcal K=\{f_1,\ldots,f_k\}\). For each \(j\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\) and \(i\in\{1,\ldots,k\}\), add vertices \(a_{ji},b_{ji}\), add a center \(c_j\), and use directed arcs \(a_{ji}\to f_i\), \(a_{ji}\to b_{ji}\), and \(b_{ji}\to c_j\). Add \(M\) private in-neighbors of each \(f_i\). The resulting WRI conflict graph consists of triangles \(\{f_i,a_{ji},b_{ji}\}\), edges \(b_{ji}c_j\), and the private core leaves.

definitions.name: Balanced restricted difference in means
definitions.construction: Given \(S_{\ell}\) of size \(K_{\ell}\), draw \(T_{\ell}\) uniformly among its \(t(K_{\ell})\)-subsets, put \(U_{\ell}=S_{\ell}\setminus T_{\ell}\), assign exposure \(\mathbf 1_{D_i}\) to every \(i\in T_{\ell}\) and \(\mathbf 0_{D_i}\) to every \(i\in U_{\ell}\), and compute \(\widehat\tau_{\ell}=e_{\ell}^{\mathsf T}\theta\).

definitions.name: Tagged-polynomial risk reconstruction
definitions.construction: Put \(p_{\ell i}(r)=[z^r]F_{\ell,\{i\}}(z)\), \(p_{\ell ij}(r)=[z^r]F_{\ell,\{i,j\}}(z)\), \(\rho_{\ell i}=\sum_{r=2}^np_{\ell i}(r)/r\), and \(m_{\ell}=(\rho_{\ell}^{\mathsf T},-\rho_{\ell}^{\mathsf T})^{\mathsf T}\). Define \(M_{\ell}^{11}(i,i)=\sum_rp_{\ell i}(r)/(r t(r))\), \(M_{\ell}^{00}(i,i)=\sum_rp_{\ell i}(r)/(r c(r))\), and, for \(i\ne j\), \(M_{\ell}^{11}(i,j)=\sum_rp_{\ell ij}(r)(t(r)-1)/(t(r)r(r-1))\), \(M_{\ell}^{00}(i,j)=\sum_rp_{\ell ij}(r)(c(r)-1)/(c(r)r(r-1))\), \(M_{\ell}^{10}(i,j)=-\sum_rp_{\ell ij}(r)/(r(r-1))\), with \(M_{\ell}^{10}(i,i)=0\) and \(M_{\ell}^{01}=(M_{\ell}^{10})^{\mathsf T}\). Set \(M_{\ell}=\begin{psmallmatrix}M_{\ell}^{11}&M_{\ell}^{10}\\M_{\ell}^{01}&M_{\ell}^{00}\end{psmallmatrix}\) and \(Q_{\ell}=M_{\ell}-m_{\ell}d^{\mathsf T}-dm_{\ell}^{\mathsf T}+dd^{\mathsf T}\).

definitions.name: Graph-Sobolev endpoint class
definitions.construction: \(\Theta_G(B)=\{\vartheta\in\mathbb R^{2n}:\vartheta^{\mathsf T}H^{-1}\vartheta\le B^2\}\), for every integer \(n\ge2\).

definitions.name: Finite-library ellipsoidal risk game
definitions.construction: Primal: \(\min_{q\in\Delta_L,t\in\mathbb R}B^2t\) subject to \(Q(q)\preceq tH^{-1}\). Dual: \(\max_{X\succeq0,s\in\mathbb R}B^2s\) subject to \(\operatorname{tr}(H^{-1}X)=1\) and \(\operatorname{tr}(Q_{\ell}X)\ge s\) for every \(\ell\).

definitions.name: Rational near-minimax certificate
definitions.construction: A tuple \((\widehat q,\widehat t,\widehat X,\widehat s)\in\mathbb Q^L\times\mathbb Q\times\mathbb Q^{2n\times2n}\times\mathbb Q\) satisfying \(\widehat q\ge0\), \(\mathbf 1_L^{\mathsf T}\widehat q=1\), \(\widehat tH^{-1}-Q(\widehat q)\succeq0\), \(\widehat X\succeq0\), \(\operatorname{tr}(H^{-1}\widehat X)=1\), \(\operatorname{tr}(Q_{\ell}\widehat X)\ge\widehat s\) for every \(\ell\), and \(B^2(\widehat t-\widehat s)\le\varepsilon\).

statements.statement: For every strict priority order \(\pi_{\ell}\), a set \(S\subseteq V\) is the WRI greedy output if and only if \(S\) is independent in \(C_G\) and every \(v\in V\setminus S\) has a neighbor \(u\in S\) that precedes \(v\) in \(\pi_{\ell}\).
statements.justification: The certificate replaces a history-dependent scan by independence and earlier-neighbor domination constraints.
statements.gap: Random sequential adsorption uses the same greedy mechanism, but the cited work does not formulate this certificate for heterogeneous tagged exact integration.
statements.consumer: The core inclusion-exclusion argument uses the certificate to separate forest components after conditioning on core priorities.

statements.statement: For every feedback-core input and every tag \(A\) with \(|A|\le2\), the exact tagged polynomial satisfies \(F_{\ell,A}(z)=\mathcal R_{\ell,A}(z)\), where \(\mathcal R_{\ell,A}\) is the evaluated target specified in \(\texttt{def:core-inclusion-exclusion}\). The identity uses at most \(3^k\) pairs \((\mathcal U,\mathcal B)\) before core-order chamber decomposition.
statements.justification: The identity removes the need to carry a subset of already satisfied core blockers through every forest message.
statements.gap: The parent proposal closes only unconditional forests; Pippenger-style scalar occupation recursions do not include core domination inclusion-exclusion or tags.
statements.consumer: Any exact feedback-parameterized oracle can work on the displayed cutoff forest rather than on the original cyclic graph.

statements.statement: If the supplied \(\mathcal K\) is a vertex cover of \(C_G\), then all \(F_{\ell,A}(z)\) with \(|A|\le2\) are computable exactly in \(Lk!3^k\operatorname{poly}(n,b,\lambda)\) bit operations, and every intermediate rational has bit length \(2^{O(k\log(k+1))}\operatorname{poly}(n,b,\lambda)\).
statements.justification: This complete special case checks the core chamber integration and bit model before heterogeneous tree branching is introduced.
statements.gap: Static vertex-cover dynamic programs do not assign weighted greedy-order probability, while the parent proposal did not prove this feedback-core chamber formula.
statements.consumer: Experiments whose cycles are concentrated on a small hub set obtain an immediate exact AWRI selection routine.

statements.statement: For \(\Gamma_{k,m,0}\) with unit noncore weights, conditional on every \(f_i\in\mathcal K\) being selected and on \(0<x_1<\cdots<x_k<1\), one component contributes \(z(\prod_{i=1}^kx_i)T_k(x)\), where \(T_k(x)=\frac1{k+1}+\sum_{r=1}^k\frac{x_r^{r+1}\prod_{i>r}x_i}{r(r+1)}\). The ordinary monomial expansion of the \(m\)-component conditional message has exactly \(\binom{m+k}{k}\) nonzero coefficients.
statements.justification: The family proves that relative core order and dense monomial expansion are both insufficient descriptions of the numerical cutoff dependence.
statements.gap: Neither static independent-set counting nor scalar adsorption recursions exhibit this finite heterogeneous core-priority support obstruction.
statements.consumer: The obstruction rejects any proposed FPT invariant that materializes all \(k\)-coordinate degree totals.

statements.statement: For \(\Gamma_{k,m,M}\) with unit noncore weights and arbitrary positive integer core weights, the probability that every core vertex is selected is computable in \(O(k!km^2)\) rational operations and \(2^{O(k\log(k+1))}\operatorname{poly}(n,b,\lambda)\) bit operations. On a chamber ordered by \(\sigma\), put \(H_r=\sum_{i=1}^r h_{\ell,\sigma(i)}\), \(\beta_r=H_r+r(M+m)-1\), \(c_0=1/(k+1)\), and \(c_r=1/(r(r+1))\). The ordered-ratio integral is evaluated by \(V_1(q)=c_1^q\), \(V_j(r)=\sum_{q=0}^r\binom rq c_j^{r-q}V_{j-1}(q)/(\beta_{j-1}+jq+1)\), and \(I_\sigma=\sum_{q=0}^m\binom mq c_0^{m-q}V_k(q)/(\beta_k+(k+1)q+1)\).
statements.justification: The recurrence demonstrates that exponentially dense conditional polynomials can still admit direct evaluated integration with only a linear moment index.
statements.gap: Gamarnik--Goldberg obtain distributional bonus recursions for limiting weighted greedy performance, not this exact finite core-conditioned coefficient and its rational bit bound.
statements.consumer: The recurrence is the technique donor and positive control for the heterogeneous moment-algebra construction.

statements.statement: For every rule \(\ell\), \(\widehat\tau_{\ell}-\tau=a_{\ell}^{\mathsf T}\theta\) and \(\mathbb E_{\ell}[(\widehat\tau_{\ell}-\tau)^2]=\theta^{\mathsf T}Q_{\ell}\theta\).
statements.justification: The quadratic retains selection bias, random denominators, and assignment variance in one design-computable object.
statements.gap: Shi, Yang, Qin, and Li bound RDIM mean squared error by a surrogate rather than state the exact endpoint quadratic.
statements.consumer: Exact graph-only rule selection needs a loss matrix that remains valid for heterogeneous fixed potential outcomes.

statements.statement: Under nondegenerate isolation, the construction in \(\texttt{def:tagged-risk-functional}\) equals \(Q_{\ell}=\mathbb E_{\ell}[a_{\ell}a_{\ell}^{\mathsf T}]\) for every \(\ell\). Thus every dense rational RDIM risk matrix is determined by tagged polynomials with tag size at most two and can be reconstructed in \(O(n^3)\) rational operations with polynomial output bit length.
statements.justification: The proposition identifies exactly which marked combinatorial moments the algorithm must compute and prevents substitution of an unmarked size law.
statements.gap: The published WRI analysis does not recover pair-specific bias and covariance from its isolated-set law.
statements.consumer: The matrix is the exact input to the finite-library minimax design certificate.

statements.statement: Construct and characterize an evaluated representation implementing \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{mom}}\) such that every cutoff-forest message remains closed under arbitrary heterogeneous branching, forest-component products, moving endpoints at ordered core priorities, and zero-, one-, and two-tagged coefficient extraction, while its state count, arithmetic count, and intermediate rational bit height are each bounded by \(2^{O(k\log(k+1))}\operatorname{poly}(n,b,\lambda)\). The representation must match exact residual enumeration on every \(\Gamma_{k,m,M}\) instance with \(k\le3\), \(m\le2\), branch weights in \(\{1,2\}\), and all admissible tags, and it must have a symbolic arbitrary-\(k,m\) complexity proof.
statements.justification: This operator closure is the sole nonstandard and genuinely open step between the exact core identity and a feedback-parameterized risk oracle.
statements.gap: Existing tree recursions are scalar, and existing structural dynamic programs do not evaluate multivariate moving-boundary priority integrals with a fixed-parameter bit bound.
statements.consumer: A solution immediately supplies exact WRI rule risks on any measured conflict graph with a small supplied feedback set.

statements.statement: There is a deterministic Turing-model algorithm that, for every input in \(\mathfrak C_k\), outputs every coefficient of every \(F_{\ell,A}(z)\) with \(|A|\le2\) and, under nondegenerate isolation, every entry of every \(Q_{\ell}\), using \(Ln^2 2^{O(k\log(k+1))}\operatorname{poly}(n,b,\lambda)\) bit operations. The algorithm contains no table of size \((nb)^k\), no unevaluated integral, and every intermediate rational has \(2^{O(k\log(k+1))}\operatorname{poly}(n,b,\lambda)\) bit length.
statements.justification: The theorem turns a simulation-chosen network design into an exactly evaluable rule library on a broad cyclic graph class.
statements.gap: Shi, Yang, Qin, and Li simulate a surrogate; random sequential adsorption gives scalar tree occupation; static independent-set algorithms omit greedy-order probabilities. None supplies this exact feedback-core oracle.
statements.consumer: After measuring the feedback number, investigators can compare candidate AWRI priority rules before a rural-China insurance-diffusion follow-up.

statements.statement: Given the exact rational matrices \(Q_1,\ldots,Q_L\) and rational \(\varepsilon>0\), a Turing-model algorithm computes a rational certificate \((\widehat q,\widehat t,\widehat X,\widehat s)\) satisfying \(\texttt{def:rational-gap-certificate}\) in time polynomial in \(L\), \(n\), \(\Lambda\), and \(\log(1/\varepsilon)\). Exact rational arithmetic verifies the simplex, trace, rule inequalities, and positive-semidefinite constraints, and weak duality certifies \(B^2\widehat s\le V^\star\le B^2\widehat t\) with gap at most \(\varepsilon\).
statements.justification: The certificate makes near-optimal rule mixing archivable without claiming an exact real-algebraic optimizer.
statements.gap: Kallus establishes the role of randomization and Duarte, Sagnol, and Wong use semidefinite minimax design, but neither produces this exact WRI and RDIM rational risk-gap certificate.
statements.consumer: A trial team can select or mix prespecified AWRI rules and independently audit the worst-case risk gap before assignment.

statements.statement: When \(k=0\), the cutoff construction reduces extensionally to the ordinary three-state forest recurrence. When \(C_G\) has no edges, \(S_{\ell}=V\) for every rule and the RDIM construction reduces to balanced complete randomization on all \(n\) units.
statements.justification: The reduction checks both the new algorithmic boundary and the classical experimental-design limit.
statements.gap: The feedback-core proposal must recover the parent's forest recurrence and cannot alter RDIM on an interference-free graph.
statements.consumer: Implementers obtain regression tests at \(k=0\) and at the no-interference design.

sampling_model.design: The graph and potential outcomes are fixed. A rule draws independent heterogeneous Beta priorities, forms a greedy maximal independent focal set, and applies balanced complete randomization within that set.
sampling_model.units: The \(n\) units, directed network, exposure domains, supplied feedback set, rule library, and endpoint schedule are fixed finite-population objects.
sampling_model.treatment: Treated focal neighborhoods receive universal treatment and control focal neighborhoods receive universal control; isolation makes these focal exposures jointly feasible.
sampling_model.overlap: Every priority order under every library rule yields at least two focal units, so both RDIM denominators are positive.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: None. The risk matrices are exact functionals of the known graph and randomization law; field outcomes are not used to choose the rule.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 4.1 bounds RDIM mean squared error by degree-distribution discrepancies and reciprocal isolated-arm sizes, and Algorithm 4 evaluates its surrogate by simulation.
Random sequential adsorption yields dynamic occupation probabilities and jamming limits on regular tree-like and restricted cyclic graph families.
A rooted-tree bonus recursion yields limiting expected weighted greedy independent-set performance and finite-girth corrections on regular graphs.
All-size static independent-set counts on treewidth-\(p\) graphs are computable in \(O(2^p p n^3)\) time.
The unrestricted design-and-estimator minimax risk is a function of the exposure conflict graph and admits graph-structural upper and lower bounds.
Randomization is minimax-variance optimal in a two-arm experimental-design game under permutation-symmetric outcome structure.
Semidefinite programming supports minimax optimal design for discretized design spaces and semidefinite-representable criteria.
Local convergence and rooted-tree equations determine asymptotic random-greedy independent-set densities for broad graph sequences.
Finite-state properties on recursively constructed graph families can be compiled into linear-time dynamic programs.
Subset Feedback Vertex Set is solvable in \(2^{O(k\log k)}n^{O(1)}\) time.
Weak convex optimization over rational well-bounded bodies has oracle-polynomial complexity with logarithmic dependence on requested accuracy.
Exposure-probability estimators under general interference admit consistency and asymptotic normality under local dependence conditions.

tldr: Weighted random isolation creates exposure-compatible focal units under network interference, but the published AWRI procedure selects priority weights by simulation because its design risk is analytically difficult. Conditional on a supplied size-\(k\) feedback vertex set of the conflict graph, a three-state forest recursion and a \(3^k\) core inclusion-exclusion identity reduce every zero-, one-, and two-tagged isolated-count law to heterogeneous cutoff-forest integrals. The paper's theorem-level kernel is an evaluated ordered-ratio moment algebra that closes those integrals under branching, component products, moving endpoints, tags, and rational coefficient extraction in \(Ln^2 2^{O(k\log(k+1))}\operatorname{poly}(n,b,\lambda)\) bit operations. Exact tagged moments reconstruct each dense RDIM risk matrix, after which a standard but explicit weak semidefinite routine returns a rational \(\varepsilon\)-minimax primal-dual certificate for the finite rule library.

project_justification.gap: AWRI fixes the relevant weighted greedy design and RDIM estimator but simulates a surrogate. Random sequential adsorption treats scalar occupation, and structural graph dynamic programs count static sets. None evaluates all heterogeneous tagged greedy moments around a feedback core with a fixed-parameter bit bound.
project_justification.niche: Conflict graphs with a small measured feedback set retain meaningful cycles and heterogeneous branch attachments while exposing a forest decomposition strong enough to support exact pre-experiment computation.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the core inclusion-exclusion identity, derives an evaluated cutoff-forest moment algebra with polynomial intermediate height, reconstructs exact RDIM risks, and emits an independently verifiable rational near-minimax certificate without an exact algebraic optimizer.

related_work: Shi, Yang, Qin, and Li define WRI and RDIM, derive a balance and inverse-size MSE surrogate, and use simulation for candidate-weight selection; their setup and motivation arc determine the causal-design objects here, but their theorem is treated as an input rather than a result to sharpen. Pippenger derives dynamic random-sequential-adsorption occupation probabilities on regular tree-like graphs, while Gamarnik and Goldberg use rooted-tree bonus recursions for expected weighted greedy performance; their subtree conditioning motivates the cutoff messages but does not provide finite heterogeneous tagged moments. Krivelevich, Meszaros, Michaeli, and Shikhelman connect random greedy independent sets to local limits and tree recursions, not exact finite feedback-core integration. Wan, Tu, Zhang, and Li compute static independent-set counts of every size on bounded-treewidth graphs, and Borie, Parker, and Tovey formalize finite-state decomposition algorithms; neither probability-weights maximal independent sets by all heterogeneous priority orders. Cygan, Pilipczuk, Pilipczuk, and Wojtaszczyk establish the relevant \(2^{O(k\log k)}\) parameterized scale for a feedback-set problem but do not supply a counting meta-theorem. Kandiros, Harshaw, and Savje characterize a different unrestricted network-experiment minimax problem through the conflict graph and graph-structural rate bounds; no equality or tightening relative to their unrestricted functional is claimed. Kallus explains mixed minimax experimental design, Duarte, Sagnol, and Wong provide a semidefinite minimax-design method, and Groetschel, Lovasz, and Schrijver provide weak rational convex optimization; these sources inform the downstream certificate. Aronow and Samii supply the standard design-based interference framework. Cai, de Janvry, and Sadoulet provide the rural-China insurance-diffusion setting, not evidence that its measured graph has small feedback number.
technical_internal_limitation: The unresolved step is not the \(3^k\) inclusion-exclusion identity, the vertex-cover case, the identical replicated-star recurrence, tagged RDIM reconstruction, or the semidefinite gap identity. It is closure of an evaluated representation for heterogeneous cutoff forests. On two components with branch-weight profiles \((1,1)\) and \((1,2)\), equal activation counts and equal current exponents can leave different exponents on the next ordered-ratio variable; relative core order, scalar activation counts, and unordered component signatures are therefore invalid states. A successful construction must first match every prescribed small replicated-star tag and the private-leaf coefficient encoding, then prove symbolic arbitrary-\(k,m\) complexity. If closure still indexes \(k\) degree totals or a profile-count vector with an \(n\)-dependent exponent, the positive kernel must be abandoned rather than restated as a circuit with an integration gate.
honest_scope: The feedback-core exact-risk theorem and the heterogeneous moment closure are open proof obligations. The supplied presolve derivations provide concrete traction but are not treated as established results. The theorem assumes a supplied feedback set and positive integer priority weights; it does not find a minimum feedback set, handle arbitrary encoded real weights, or claim that the rural-China graph has small feedback number. The minimax result chooses within a prespecified WRI and RDIM library under a graph-Sobolev endpoint ellipsoid; it does not equal the unrestricted all-design, all-estimator minimax functional of Kandiros, Harshaw, and Savje. At \(k=0\) the construction must reproduce the known forest recurrence, and on an empty conflict graph it must reproduce balanced complete randomization.

seed_details.title: Evaluated feedback-core algebra for exact WRI and RDIM risk
seed_details.anchor_location: Algorithm 3, Theorem 4.1, Appendix S2.1, Section 4.2, and Section 6
seed_details.opened_evidence: Algorithm 3 fixes weighted sequential random isolation; Theorem 4.1 and Appendix S2.1 bound RDIM mean squared error by balance and reciprocal-size terms; Section 4.2 simulates the resulting surrogate because its analytical evaluation is complicated; Section 6 asks for stronger theory and effective probability approximation.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Conditioning on a supplied feedback set creates numerical core cutoffs in otherwise independent forest components. The missing theorem is an evaluated representation that closes under heterogeneous child products, moving endpoints, component products, and every tag while avoiding a table with an exponent depending on \(k\).
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the scalar time-indexed occupation message used on a tree by a core-conditioned operator message that preserves the future ordered-ratio exponent profile when distinct branches attach to distinct subsets of the core.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches combining weighted random isolation, greedy maximal independent sets, feedback vertex number, exact tagged moments, and priority-order integration found tree occupation recursions and static bounded-treewidth counting, but no exact weighted tagged greedy-law algorithm parameterized by feedback vertex number.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from bounded-treewidth dynamic programming because independent sets and their size polynomial are already fixed-parameter tractable.
seed_details.rebuttal: Static independent-set counts assign one weight per set, whereas WRI assigns the total probability mass of all priority orders producing that set; heterogeneous core cutoffs retain numerical order information that ordinary bag states discard.

seed_details.title: Rational near-minimax certificate for a finite WRI rule library
seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction, the informal main result, Section 6, Appendix A, and Conclusion
seed_details.opened_evidence: The paper makes the conflict graph the design-based minimax object and bounds the unrestricted design-and-estimator risk; its Introduction calls the exact graph functional complicated, while its Conclusion identifies computational complexity as open. It does not give a rational certificate for a prespecified WRI and RDIM library.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Given exact rational rule matrices, turn the ellipsoidal worst-case risk into primal and dual spectral epigraphs and return rational feasible points with a directly checkable gap, without asserting that an exact optimizer is rational.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the unsupported exact real-algebraic optimizer by weak rational semidefinite optimization, strict-feasibility erosion, affine repair, and outward objective rounding.
seed_details.destination_search: Kallus supplies the zero-sum role of mixed experimental designs, Duarte, Sagnol, and Wong supply semidefinite minimax-design machinery, and Groetschel, Lovasz, and Schrijver supply weak rational convex optimization; none begins with exact WRI and RDIM risk matrices or emits this certificate.
seed_details.red_team: Once the matrices are known, this is merely a standard semidefinite program.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection limits its novelty, so the certificate is retained as a downstream deliverable rather than the tier-bearing kernel; its value is to make exact risk computation operational and independently auditable.

seed_details.title: Design-based RDIM limit law after graph-only WRI rule selection
seed_details.anchor_location: The seed named \(\texttt{seed-wri-limit-law}\), its first changed proof step, and the terminal scope discussion
seed_details.opened_evidence: The prior proposal records that conditioning on the isolated set leaves unresolved the unconditioning over a global greedy support and random reciprocal denominators. The source paper supplies simulation evidence but no studentized design-based central limit theorem.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Show that conditioning on finitely many feedback-core states localizes forest support changes strongly enough for a uniform conditional-to-unconditional central limit theorem and a conservative or consistent studentizer.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Before invoking a dependency-graph or Stein argument, prove a quantitative stabilization radius for WRI inclusion indicators after the core priorities and the graph-only selected rule are fixed.
seed_details.destination_search: Aronow and Samii prove asymptotic normality from local exposure dependence, Leung proves approximate-neighborhood-interference normality with network HAC inference, and Krivelevich, M\'esz\'aros, Michaeli, and Shikhelman prove local-limit control for random greedy independent sets; none covers RDIM with a generated weighted greedy support and random denominators after rule selection.
seed_details.red_team: Condition on the isolated set and apply the complete-randomization central limit theorem.
seed_details.rebuttal: The conditional centering varies with a globally selected and potentially unrepresentative support, and the random arm denominators can fail to stabilize; neither issue disappears after conditioning.

seed_details.title: Parameterized hardness of one risk-determining WRI coefficient
seed_details.anchor_location: General review improvement directive and the abandoned hardness seed in the proposal core
seed_details.opened_evidence: The prior review demands a parameter-preserving hardness reduction, while the prior seed admits that its poset flower does not encode greedy domination and provides no coefficient-recovery identity.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Construct a domination gadget whose single one- or two-tagged coefficient recovers a standard parameterized source count while the feedback vertex number depends only on the source parameter.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Translate a source order constraint into the existence of an earlier selected neighbor, rather than importing a poset comparability gadget that has no greedy-domination semantics.
seed_details.destination_search: The closest order-counting hardness result concerns cover-graph treewidth, not WRI feedback vertex number; no source problem and gadget with the required parameter map was located.
seed_details.red_team: Counting linear extensions is already hard at bounded cover-graph width, so the WRI claim follows.
seed_details.rebuttal: A priority order accepted by WRI is characterized by independent domination, not by transitive order constraints; without a reduction the comparator gives only warning, not hardness.
seed_details.disposition: dropped because the positive construction has substantially stronger traction

seed_details.title: Ordered-ratio closure for heterogeneous replicated-star integrals
seed_details.anchor_location: The feedback-core presolve, Sections 4 and 5.2, and the parent technical limitation
seed_details.opened_evidence: The presolve derives a directed-realizable replicated-star family with dense conditional support, proves a scalar ordered-ratio recurrence for identical attachments, and exhibits two heterogeneous profiles that defeat activation-count compression. The parent technical limitation states that finite width checks cannot establish fixed-parameter tractability.
seed_details.proof_boundary: For the directed-realizable replicated-star family, compress a product of heterogeneous core-coupled component factors into nested moments with state size depending only exponentially on \(k\) and polynomially on the number of branches.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace one scalar occupation message by an ordered-ratio operator that carries the full future prefix-weight profile created when a heterogeneous branch term activates.
seed_details.destination_search: The search found scalar or distributional tree recursions and exact one-dimensional adsorption laws, but no symbolic arbitrary-\(k,m\) evaluation of these heterogeneous core-boundary integrals.
seed_details.red_team: The ordered-ratio recurrence for identical attachments extends by simply recording the number of activated branches.
seed_details.rebuttal: Two branches with profiles \((1,1)\) and \((1,2)\) can have the same current activation count and exponent but different future exponents, so scalar activation is not a sufficient state.
seed_details.disposition: absorbed as the mandatory first test of the selected seed

seed_details.title: Exact evaluation of the published AWRI surrogate on feedback-small graphs
seed_details.anchor_location: Theorem 4.1, Equation defining \(\mathcal M(\mathbf w)\), and Algorithm 4
seed_details.opened_evidence: The paper's selection rule minimizes a simulated degree-balance and reciprocal-arm-size surrogate over candidate weights. Its proof identifies exactly which isolated-set moments enter that surrogate.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Compute only the marked degree histogram and reciprocal arm-size terms, potentially permitting a smaller state than the dense RDIM risk matrix.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace Monte Carlo averages in Algorithm 4 by tagged generating-function coefficients before asking for all pairwise RDIM moments.
seed_details.destination_search: No exact bounded-feedback evaluation of the published surrogate was located, although the full selected seed would make this result a corollary.
seed_details.red_team: The full tagged-risk oracle immediately contains every surrogate moment.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds once the selected theorem is proved; the narrower oracle is therefore not an independent paper kernel.

seed_details.title: Priority-weighted independent-set polynomial on bounded treewidth
seed_details.anchor_location: Abstract and main dynamic-programming result on pages 42--47
seed_details.opened_evidence: Wan, Tu, Zhang, and Li compute the number of independent sets of every size on a graph of treewidth \(p\) in \(O(2^p p n^3)\) time. Their objective is a static cardinality count and contains no priority-order probability.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Define and compute the generating polynomial whose coefficient weights each maximal independent set by the probability that heterogeneous greedy priorities produce it.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: At a separator forget operation, integrate the forgotten priority while retaining which boundary vertices can still dominate later vertices.
seed_details.destination_search: Order-counting work indicates that multivariate separator integration may remain only XP, and no matching FPT theorem for the priority-weighted polynomial was located.
seed_details.red_team: Attach the WRI probability as a local vertex weight in the existing independent-set polynomial.
seed_details.rebuttal: The probability of a maximal independent set is a sum over compatible global orders and does not factor into vertex weights, so the static recurrence cannot be reused unchanged.
seed_details.disposition: dropped because feedback-core conditioning gives a sharper tractable interface than general treewidth

seed_details.title: Robust WRI selection over an uncertain conflict graph
seed_details.anchor_location: Conclusion discussion of weighted, noisy, and unobserved social networks
seed_details.opened_evidence: The conclusion explicitly identifies network noise and nonobservation as practical limitations, whereas the WRI construction conditions on one fixed known network.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Optimize the exact worst-case risk over a compact family of edge completions whose members share a small feedback core.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Core-conditioned forest messages must propagate unresolved edge states jointly with priority cutoffs because each completion changes both feasibility and the greedy law.
seed_details.destination_search: Robust-network methods were found for sensitivity and averaging, but not an exact WRI risk separation oracle over exponentially many feedback-small graph completions.
seed_details.red_team: Compute every candidate graph separately and maximize the resulting risk.
seed_details.rebuttal: That enumerates exponentially many completions and supplies no compact certificate; current evidence is insufficient for a credible theorem route.

seed_details.title: Exact WRI risk when the supplied feedback core is a vertex cover
seed_details.anchor_location: Forest-oracle theorem and feedback-core presolve vertex-cover branch
seed_details.opened_evidence: The parent establishes exact forest messages, and the presolve derives direct chamber integration when deleting the core leaves an edgeless graph.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Enumerate independent core selections, blocker subsets, and core orders, then integrate the resulting chamber monomials.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Outside vertices become forced by the selected core, so no heterogeneous tree branching remains.
seed_details.destination_search: The complete derivation and finite exact checks already settle this special case inside the supplied presolve evidence.
seed_details.red_team: This is no longer an open research seed because the supplied derivation already gives the algorithm.
seed_details.disposition: dropped and retained only as a theorem-level boundary check

literature_map.settled: Algorithm 3 defines heterogeneous weighted sequential isolation, Theorem 4.1 and Appendix S2.1 derive a degree-balance and inverse-size risk surrogate, and Algorithm 4 selects among candidate weights by simulation.
literature_map.open_boundary: Neither the exact tagged isolated-count law nor the dense exact RDIM risk matrix is evaluated analytically.
literature_map.used_as: Writing exemplar and fixed causal-design specification.

literature_map.thread: Random sequential adsorption and weighted greedy recursion
literature_map.settled: These papers derive scalar or distributional recursions for occupation and limiting expected greedy independent-set size on regular, high-girth, locally convergent, or tree settings.
literature_map.open_boundary: They do not compute a finite heterogeneous priority law with zero-, one-, and two-tagged count coefficients under numerical cutoffs supplied by a feedback core.
literature_map.used_as: Method exemplars for rooted-subtree conditioning and the warning that the scalar state must be enlarged.

literature_map.settled: Static independent-set counts of all sizes and many finite-state graph properties are tractable on bounded-treewidth decompositions.
literature_map.open_boundary: A heterogeneous greedy priority measure is not a static set weight, and moving-boundary integration plus intermediate rational height is absent from these algorithms.
literature_map.used_as: Closest algorithmic comparator and state-space contrast.

literature_map.settled: Subset Feedback Vertex Set admits a \(2^{O(k\log k)}n^{O(1)}\) algorithm, establishing a familiar parameterized scale for supplied feedback structure.
literature_map.open_boundary: The result is not a counting or priority-integration theorem and does not imply the requested moment algebra.

literature_map.settled: Conflict graphs determine an unrestricted design-based minimax problem, and mixed randomization is a legitimate zero-sum design decision.
literature_map.open_boundary: The unrestricted functional is not the finite WRI and RDIM library game, and neither paper emits a rational primal-dual certificate from exact rule matrices.

literature_map.thread: Semidefinite minimax optimization and weak rational certification
literature_map.settled: Finite minimax design criteria can be written with semidefinite epigraphs, and weak convex optimization over rational well-bounded bodies returns rational approximate solutions with logarithmic accuracy dependence.
literature_map.open_boundary: The WRI application still requires explicit strict seeds, exact affine and positive-semidefinite feasibility checks, repair, and outward rounding tied to its risk gap.
literature_map.used_as: Method exemplar for the non-algebraic certificate.

literature_map.settled: Exposure estimators admit consistency and normal approximation under local or decaying network dependence, with exposure-probability variance accounting or network HAC inference.
literature_map.open_boundary: Those estimators do not first generate a weighted greedy focal support with random reciprocal arm counts and then select a rule using the graph.
literature_map.used_as: Adjacent inference thread confirming a missing stabilization lemma.

literature_map.settled: Local-limit and bonus-recursion arguments control greedy inclusion on trees and locally tree-like graph sequences and yield expected-size or concentration results.
literature_map.open_boundary: A uniform design-based central limit theorem for RDIM requires localization of marked membership, centering, and denominators after graph-only rule selection.
literature_map.used_as: Candidate proof donor; not used by the selected kernel beyond the common tree recursion.

novelty_justification: The closest design paper is Shi, Yang, Qin, and Li: it fixes the WRI and RDIM objects but replaces analytical evaluation of its risk surrogate by simulation. The closest combinatorial papers are Pippenger and Gamarnik--Goldberg, whose tree recursions target scalar occupation or limiting expected size, and Wan, Tu, Zhang, and Li, whose dynamic program counts static independent sets. None evaluates the finite heterogeneous priority measure after conditioning on a feedback core, preserves every one- and two-tagged count coefficient, proves polynomial intermediate rational height, and reconstructs the dense RDIM risk matrix in fixed-parameter bit complexity. Kandiros, Harshaw, and Savje optimize over all designs and estimators through a different implicit conflict-graph functional; the present kernel makes no claim to compute or tighten that unrestricted minimax value. Its theorem concerns an exact, prespecified WRI and RDIM library. The bounded searches covered the exact target--method pair and adjacent priority-order, treewidth, random sequential adsorption, and network-design literatures; no closer result subsuming the kernel was located.
